figures.Fig16.3: Hormones of anterior & posterior pituitary and their target sites (PDF page 62). Original figure archived as c12-bio-ch16-fig-16-3-pituitary-targets (drawn for this lesson after the printed figure; not the textbook's picture). The printed figure shows the GH and prolactin arrows (anterior pituitary hormones) leaving from beneath the posterior lobe; drawn with every anterior hormone leaving the anterior lobe (correct).

findings: The book writes 'cortisone' for the corticosteroids stimulated by ACTH; cortisol is the main glucocorticoid (the book itself uses cortisol later). The lesson says corticosteroids, flagged.
The Tidbit on growth hormone treatment and the For Information boxes on the origin of the posterior pituitary and on breast-feeding are carried in the lesson.

Owner rule (2026-10-21): the English lesson carries only the book's content. Our explanations, notes on the print, self-check questions with their answers, the recap, 3D models and figures the book does not print are in the Roman Urdu lesson only; where the book's own Quick Check or Brain Teaser questions are given, the English lesson lists them without answers.

Figure 16.3 draws the GH and prolactin arrows from under the posterior pituitary, although both are anterior pituitary hormones (as the text says). The drawing starts them at the anterior lobe and the Roman Urdu tip box explains it.

Figure book error (c12-bio-ch16-fig-16-3-pituitary-targets): drawn correctly; English Book correction box after the figure: The printed Figure 16.3 draws the GH and prolactin arrows from beneath the posterior lobe; both are hormones of the anterior pituitary, so the drawing above takes them from the anterior lobe.
